International Day of Peace 
UMass Dartmouth proudly observed the 
International Day of Peace on September 
18th, joining communities around the world 
in recognizing the importance of unity, 
nonviolence, and mutual understanding. This 
day, established by the United Nations, serves 
as a reminder of our shared responsibility to 
foster peace both globally and locally. 
Students, faculty, and staff gathered to reflect 
on the meaning of peace and the importance 
of fostering an inclusive community. The event 
featured the re-dedication of the UMass 
Dartmouth Peace Pole, where participants 
shared the message "May Peace Prevail on 
Earth" in different languages, celebrating unity 
and cultural diversity. 
The celebration was organized in collaboration 
with the Leduc Center for Civic Engagement, 
Frederick Douglass Unity House, Center 
for Religious & Spiritual Life, Model UN, 
International Student & Scholar Center, and 
Nepali Students' Association. 
By creating spaces where diverse voices are 
heard and respected, UMass Dartmouth 
continues to strengthen its commitment to 
civic engagement, social justice, and a culture 
of care. 
World Central Kitchen Fundraiser 
Following the International Day of Peace, the Leduc Center for Civic Engagement launched a campus-wide 
fundraiser in support of World Central Kitchen (WCK), the nonprofit organization founded by chef José Andrés. 
WCK provides fresh, nourishing meals to communities impacted by natural disasters, climate-related events, 
and humanitarian crises across the globe. Operating on the frontlines of emergencies, the organization is 
recognized for its rapid response efforts and its commitment to ensuring that food is accessible to those in 
urgent need. 
From September 21st through November 25th, the UMass Dartmouth community came together in support of 
this effort, raising a total of $1,485 to contribute to WCK’s global relief work.
